decisions.why: best after 1 auction call(s); C 186,560 below the limit 214,296

key_points: Leverage RFQ for a new part with no current price: two new suppliers compete, award one. Our alternative is a quote at the fallback price on DAP, sixty days and thirty-five days lead time.

The evidence is thin: there are no dossiers, and the only arguments are general market news, almost all of which argue the supplier's side (steel, labour, alloy). The one for-us item is power prices, which is context only and weak for machining.

The case refs (should-cost for SH-220, both supplier scorecards, forecast, news N-0412) are not in the argument lists, so our main lever is price movement plus honest competition between the two bids.
Lead time is a must-have of at most forty-two days, and every day beyond thirty-five costs EUR 150 per day. Ask for thirty-five days and do not push shorter, so we avoid a price penalty.

Keep fourteen-day payment as the closing trade if a supplier signals cash need. DAP is preferred, because freight under EXW/FCA from Poland adds cost; FCA can be offered only if it comes priced lower.
Step upward each round in shrinking steps and keep the second supplier warm until award.
plan.stance_why: This is a competitive leverage RFQ with two eager new suppliers and a priced alternative, so a deep anchor is warranted. Avoid adding costly demands such as very short lead times.

levers.why: This is the only for-us record. It is context-level and weak, but usable as a single fresh fact in a later round to offset energy-cost claims.

argument.note: 2026-09-12 market: Industrial power prices -43 % on 2022. Producer prices for electric power stand -43 % against August 2022. Do not cite it as about this supplier.

trades.why: Thirty-five days matches our need and avoids delay cost without pushing for a costly shorter lead time.
DAP keeps freight with a domestic supplier, where it is cheap for them.
Fourteen days is worth a final price step if they show cash need, and the interest cost to us is small.

sup:DEMO-J1.opening_paragraph: Thank you for your quotation for the stainless shaft of our new pump series. We value a nearby partner who can support the launch reliably. We are comparing offers on total cost, delivery and terms, and would like to build a lasting relationship with the supplier we award. Please find our proposal attached.
watch_for: Steel or labour cost claims: answer with a priced step rather than debate
Final offer wording: accept it or take an alternative sheet in the same e-mail
Lead time quoted above forty-two days

levers.why: Context-only filler. Use it once and only if a fresh fact is needed.

argument.note: 2026-09-12 market: Industrial power prices -43 % on 2022. Producer prices for electric power stand -43 % against August 2022. Do not cite it as about this supplier.

trades.why: Cross-border freight and delivery risk should sit with the supplier, so absolute costs are comparable.
Thirty-five days fits our line need, including transit.
This is a likely cash-need lever for a growing exporter, so keep it for the last step.

sup:DEMO-C1.opening_paragraph: Thank you for your offer for the stainless shaft of our new pump series. We appreciate your interest in working with us and see real potential in a long-term partnership. We compare offers on total delivered cost and reliable supply to our plant, and look forward to your view on our proposal.
watch_for: Transit time pushing delivered lead time past forty-two days
Freight-term switching to EXW/FCA that hides cost

risks: There are no verifiable for-us records, so concessions depend on our price steps and competition alone.
An aggressive anchor may trigger an early final offer.
Lead time breaches would cost EUR 150 per day, or make a bid noncompliant.
Freight cost for the Polish supplier is unknown and could tip the comparison.
Citing for-them market news would hand them arguments.
